territory: Profile and settings surfaces: src/components/settings/actions.ts + theme-actions.ts + avatar-crop-dialog, src/components/profile/* (profile-actions, letterhead-profile, contacts-editor, house-chain-editor, houses-chain, pen, saved-posts-feed, profile-author-feed, get-in-touch, flag-person-dialog, admin-actions), src/app/(main)/profile/[id]/page.tsx, src/lib/{avatar,theme,house-spans,houses,mask-email,account-purge,retention,social,normalize}.ts, src/app/api/account/export/route.ts, src/app/(main)/dark-mode, plus the JSON-in-string columns (houses/phones/links), the deletion request→grace→purge path, and the avatar change flow.

findings.title: Removing a contact row saves the pre-removal list: commitContacts reads a stale contactRows closure, so the removed phone/link/email silently survives in the DB
findings.expected: Clicking the X on a contact row removes that phone number / link / social from the member's stored contact methods.
findings.actual: The UI removes the row, but the server write persists the OLD list including the removed row. On the next page load the 'removed' phone number is back on the member's public Get in touch sheet.
findings.evidence: contacts-editor.tsx remove button (lines 226-229): `onClick={() => { onChange(rows.filter((r) => r.id !== row.id)); onCommit(); }}`. `onChange` is `setContactRows` and `onCommit` is `commitContacts` from letterhead-profile.tsx:423-429: `function commitContacts() { void run(async () => { const result = await updateContactMethods(rowsToPayload(contactRows)); ... }) }`. `commitContacts` closes over the `contactRows` state variable of the render in which the click happened — `setContactRows(next)` has not re-rendered yet when `onCommit()` executes in the same event handler, so `rowsToPayload(contactRows)` serialises the PRE-removal array and `updateContactMethods` writes it. The success then calls `router.refresh()`, but the client `contactRows` state (initialised once in `useState(() => draft ? buildRows(draft.contacts) : [])`, letterhead-profile.tsx:332-334) is preserved across refresh, so the UI keeps showing the row as gone while the DB still has it. The blur-commit path (PenValue onCommit) is safe because keystroke onChange events re-render before blur; only the same-tick onChange+onCommit of the remove button hits the stale closure. Removing a phone number is a privacy gesture: the member believes it is off their profile while every verified viewer still gets it in Get in touch and in the vCard.
findings.fixDirection: Make removal commit the list it just computed: either change ContactsEditor's remove handler to call a new `onRemove(next: ContactRow[])` prop that both sets state and saves `rowsToPayload(next)` directly, or change `commitContacts` to accept an explicit rows argument (`commitContacts(next)`) and have the remove button pass the filtered array. Same pattern commitPlaces/commitHouses already use (they pass `next` into the action).
findings.gateOrTest: New unit/component test: render ContactsEditor with two phone rows, click remove on one, assert updateContactMethods was called with a payload of ONE phone. Also a Playwright spec: remove a phone in edit mode, reload the profile, assert the number is absent from Get in touch.
findings.reproPlan: Live proof on a test account via chrome-devtools: sign in, open own profile, Edit, add two phone numbers, blur to save, click X on one, reload the page — the removed number reappears.

findings.title: A member cannot remove their email from the profile: deleting the email row saves displayEmail=null, and the page then falls back to exposing the sign-in email (and buildRows re-seeds the row on reload)
findings.expected: The email row in 'Reaching you' carries the same remove affordance as every other row; removing it should stop the profile from offering an email address (or the row should not offer removal at all).
findings.actual: Removing the email row (even when the stale-closure bug above doesn't intervene) writes displayEmail=null, after which the profile serves the member's LOGIN email to every Stage-2 viewer: page.tsx:177 `const contactEmail = user.displayEmail?.trim() || user.email;`. On next edit, buildRows (contacts-editor.tsx:126-127: `if (source.displayEmail || source.email) rows.push({ ... value: source.displayEmail || source.email })`) re-seeds the row from the account email, so the 'removed' row reappears. The X on the email row is a no-op that looks like a privacy control.
findings.evidence: The remove button renders unconditionally for every row kind (contacts-editor.tsx:223-235, no `row.kind !== "email"` guard). rowsToPayload (lines 94-106) returns `displayEmail: first("email")` = null when the row is gone; updateContactMethods (profile-actions.ts:229) stores `displayEmail: parsed.data.displayEmail || null`. The profile page and vCard then use the fallback `user.displayEmail?.trim() || user.email` (page.tsx:177, 274), so the sign-in address ships to all verified members. There is no showEmail/showPhone column in schema.prisma (grep confirms zero hits), so no opt-out exists anywhere.
findings.fixDirection: Decide the contract and make the UI honest. Either (a) email is mandatory on the sheet: drop the X on the email row (kind === "email" renders no remove button) so the affordance stops lying; or (b) support hiding: add an explicit empty-state for displayEmail (e.g. a sentinel or a showEmail boolean) that suppresses the fallback in page.tsx:177 and in the vCard, and stop buildRows re-seeding from source.email when the member explicitly cleared it.
findings.gateOrTest: Component test: buildRows/rowsToPayload round-trip with the email row removed must not resurrect an email. E2E: remove email row, reload, assert Get in touch shows no email (or assert the X is absent, per the chosen contract).
findings.reproPlan: Test account: set no displayEmail, open edit mode, observe the email row (login address) carries an X; remove it, save, view own profile as a second verified test account — email still offered.

findings.title: Account purge misses AdminMessage.imageUrl screenshots (and Group.coverImage): member deletion cascades the rows away and permanently orphans their R2 bytes at public URLs
findings.expected: purgeUserAccount's own contract (header comment: 'The one place that knows how to erase a member COMPLETELY... bytes in R2 that no cascade can reach... That is what made GDPR Art. 17 unachievable for images') collects EVERY stored-image URL the member's rows point at before the cascade destroys them.
findings.actual: collectImageUrls (account-purge.ts:37-68) reads only User.photoUrl, Post.images, Photo.{thumbUrl,url,originalUrl}, and CatchupEntry.images. It never reads AdminMessage.imageUrl ('one optional screenshot (WebP via /api/upload)', schema.prisma:587). AdminThread.member is `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:568) and AdminMessage.thread is `onDelete: Cascade` (line 590), so a deleted member's admin-thread messages — and with them the only rows pointing at their uploaded screenshots — are destroyed in the same transaction, leaving the WebP bytes publicly fetchable at their pub-*.r2.dev URLs forever with nothing able to enumerate them. (The `authorId SetNull` comment on AdminMessage only saves messages sitting in OTHER people's threads.) Same class: Group.coverImage (schema.prisma:195) with `creator ... onDelete: Cascade` (line 201) — legacy Group rows created by the member cascade away with an uncollected cover URL.
findings.evidence: account-purge.ts:38-46: `const [user, posts, photos, entries] = await Promise.all([ prisma.user.findUnique(...photoUrl...), prisma.post.findMany(...images...), prisma.photo.findMany(...), prisma.catchupEntry.findMany(...images...) ]);` — no adminMessage or group query. schema.prisma:590 `thread AdminThread @relation(... onDelete: Cascade)` + :568 `member User @relation("AdminThreadMember", ... onDelete: Cascade)` proves the member's threads and messages die with the user row.
findings.fixDirection: In collectImageUrls, add `prisma.adminMessage.findMany({ where: { thread: { memberId: userId } }, select: { imageUrl: true } })` (all messages in the member's threads, since the whole thread cascades) and, if legacy Group rows can exist, `prisma.group.findMany({ where: { creatorId: userId }, select: { coverImage: true } })`; push non-null URLs into the list. delImage already ignores URLs that are not ours, so collecting generously stays safe.
findings.gateOrTest: Extend the purge unit test (or add one): seed a user with an admin-thread message carrying imageUrl, run purgeUserAccount, assert delImage was called with that URL. A schema-audit check could also assert every String column whose comment mentions an upload URL appears in collectImageUrls.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would require deleting an account against the shared production database).

findings.title: Retention purge runs unbounded sequential R2 deletes AFTER the row cascade, inside a route with no maxDuration: a timeout mid-loop permanently orphans the remaining un-enumerable objects
findings.expected: The nightly sweep purges due accounts within the serverless duration budget, and a partial failure leaves a durable record of which R2 objects still need deleting.
findings.actual: purgeUserAccount deletes the rows first (correctly argued in its comment), then `for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; }` — one awaited DeleteObject round-trip per URL, sequential. retention.ts:115-136 loops over ALL due users (`findMany` with no take) and purges each in turn; the sweep route exports no `maxDuration` (grep across src/app finds none) so it runs at the platform default. A member with a large Collection contribution history (each Photo contributes 2-3 URLs) can push one purge into hundreds of sequential HTTP deletes; when the function times out after the row transaction has committed, the un-deleted URLs are orphaned with no row left pointing at them and no retry possible — exactly the un-enumerable-bytes failure the file's own header says it exists to prevent. The per-user audit entry and the sweep's closing 'retention.sweep' audit are also lost on timeout, so the failure is invisible in /admin/audit.
findings.evidence: account-purge.ts:108-113: `let deleted = 0; for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; } return { ok: true, imagesDeleted: deleted };` after the `prisma.$transaction([...user.delete...])` at :99-102. retention.ts:116-118: `const rows = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { deletionRequestedAt: { lt: cutoff(DELETION_GRACE_DAYS) } }, select: {...} });` — unbounded, then sequential `await purgeUserAccount(row.id)` per row.
findings.fixDirection: Two independent hardenings: (1) make the object deletions durable-or-batched — write the collected URL list into the audit detail (or a small PurgeQueue table) BEFORE the row transaction, so a timeout leaves a retryable record; and/or delete in parallel batches (Promise.allSettled over chunks of ~25, or S3 DeleteObjects batching) to cut wall time an order of magnitude. (2) export `maxDuration` on the sweep route sized to the worst case, and cap users-per-sweep (take: N) so one heavy account cannot starve the rest — the sweep is already idempotent so the remainder purges tomorrow. Note the same slow-sequential-delete shape also applies to adminDeleteUser, which shares purgeUserAccount inside a user-facing server action.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test purgeUserAccount with a mocked delImage asserting batched/parallel deletion; a test on runRetentionSweep asserting a `take` bound; verify the sweep route exports maxDuration.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (cannot exercise deletion against the shared production database); timing can be argued from delImage being one awaited S3 round-trip per URL.

findings.title: updateUserPlaces takes its input entirely on trust: no Zod, no length caps on label/city, unvalidated lat/lng/placeId — the one profile writer without the M18-standard gate
findings.expected: Every server action validates everything, including types and lengths — the standard the codebase itself set when audit M18 added contactMethodsSchema because updateContactMethods 'used to write with NO validation at all'.
findings.actual: `export async function updateUserPlaces(places: {...}[])` is a public POST whose TypeScript parameter types are erased at runtime. The body does `places.map((p) => ({ placeId: p.placeId, label: titleCase(p.label.trim()), city: titleCase(p.city.trim()), lat: p.lat, lng: p.lng }))` with only `.filter((p) => p.label.length > 0).slice(0, 30)`. Consequences: (a) a non-array or a row with non-string label throws (`p.label.trim` is not a function) — an unhandled server-action exception instead of an error result; (b) label/city have NO length cap, so a crafted call stores 30 rows x arbitrary-length strings (megabytes) which then render on the profile facts row, the directory, and the vCard for every viewer, and mirror into User.currentCity; (c) lat/lng accept any number (NaN/Infinity/out-of-range floats) flowing into map surfaces; (d) a float placeId throws a Prisma Int validation error. Storage bloat/DoS is squarely the stability class this audit owns (the 2026-08-20 security pass covered authz/injection, not resource exhaustion).
findings.evidence: settings/actions.ts:144-159 (quoted above) — contrast with updateContactMethods in profile-actions.ts:217 (`contactMethodsSchema.safeParse`) and saveOnboardingHouses in onboarding/actions.ts:140 (`housesPayloadSchema.safeParse`), the two sibling list-writers that both parse first. File is uncommitted WIP; this is its current state.
findings.fixDirection: Add a `placesSchema = z.array(z.object({ placeId: z.number().int().nullable(), label: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120), city: z.string().trim().max(100), lat: z.number().min(-90).max(90).nullable(), lng: z.number().min(-180).max(180).nullable() })).max(30)` and safeParse before the transaction, returning { error } on failure — same shape as contactMethodsSchema per M18.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test posting an over-long label and a non-numeric lat to updateUserPlaces expecting { error }, not a throw; the existing security-regressions test file is the natural home.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test account: call the action from the console with a 100k-char label; confirm today it stores and renders. (Write is to the tester's own row and reversible.)

findings.title: Whole-list autosaves race: cities and houses commit the full list on every interaction with no ordering guard, so out-of-order completion silently persists an older list
findings.expected: Rapid consecutive edits (the house chain editor deliberately 'hands the panel straight to the next year' encouraging quick successive picks; the cities picker commits on every add/remove) end with the DB holding the final list.
findings.actual: Each interaction fires an independent full-list write: commitPlaces → updateUserPlaces (deleteMany + recreate, settings/actions.ts:162-181) and commitHouses → saveOnboardingHouses (one JSON overwrite, onboarding/actions.ts:150-153). Two in-flight writes A (older list) and B (newer) can complete B-then-A — server actions are independent POSTs with no sequencing — leaving the DB with the OLDER list while the client state shows the newer one. router.refresh() re-renders the server tree but the client `houses`/`places` useState persists, so the member sees all their picks; the loss surfaces only on the next full reload (house picks vanished). Most plausible on slow mobile networks, which is the member base (India, phones). The same shape applies to two tabs editing simultaneously (delete+recreate last-writer-wins wholesale).
findings.evidence: letterhead-profile.tsx:414-421: `function commitHouses(next) { setHouses(next); void run(async () => { const result = await saveOnboardingHouses(next); ... }) }` — invoked per pick from HouseChainEditor's toggle; nothing cancels or serialises the previous in-flight save. useAutoSave's `run` (pen.tsx:348) counts overlapping calls for the spinner but does not order them.
findings.fixDirection: Serialise per-list writes client-side: keep a per-key promise chain (start the next save only after the previous settles) or a monotonically increasing sequence stamp the client checks before treating a completion as current; alternatively debounce commitHouses/commitPlaces (~600ms trailing) so rapid picks coalesce into one write. Server-side, a `updatedAt`-style optimistic check would also close the two-tab case.
findings.gateOrTest: Component test with mocked actions resolving out of order: fire two commitHouses calls, resolve the second first, assert the FINAL persisted payload equals the last-issued list.
findings.reproPlan: Live with chrome-devtools network throttling (Slow 3G) on a test account: click through 4-5 house picks quickly, hard-reload, compare the chain against what was picked.

findings.title: Auto-save failure semantics: commitField marks the value saved BEFORE the write, so a failed save can never be retried by re-blurring, and useAutoSave silently swallows an error that finishes while another save is in flight
findings.expected: A field whose save failed (network blip, transient 500) is retried the next time the member commits it; an error is always surfaced.
findings.actual: commitField (letterhead-profile.tsx:392-401): `const value = form[key]; if (saved.current[key] === value) return; saved.current[key] = value;` — the value is recorded as saved before the request runs. If updateProfileField fails, saved.current still holds the value, so blurring the same field again (the natural retry gesture) returns early and never retries; the edit is lost unless the member changes the text. Compounding it, useAutoSave (pen.tsx:360-368): `inFlight.current -= 1; if (inFlight.current > 0) return; if (failed) { setState("error"); ... }` — when save A fails while save B is still in flight, A's completion returns early (counter > 0) and B's later success paints 'Saved', so the member is shown success while field A's edit was dropped, with no error ever displayed and no retry possible.
findings.evidence: Quoted lines above; the SaveMark comment itself says 'An error stays put... because the value on screen is not the value on file' — but the mechanism only holds for the last-finishing save, and the retry path is dead either way.
findings.fixDirection: In commitField, set saved.current[key] only after a successful result (or clear it in the failure branch). In useAutoSave, track failures across the in-flight window (e.g. accumulate `failed` in a ref and report it when the counter reaches zero) so one failure among overlapping saves still shows the error state.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on a commitField-like harness: mock action fails once then succeeds; blur twice with the same value; assert two calls were made and the second persisted. Second test: two overlapping runs, first rejects, second resolves — assert final state is 'error'.
findings.reproPlan: Live with chrome-devtools: set network offline, edit About, blur (error mark appears), go back online, blur the same field again — no request fires; press Done and reload: the edit is gone.

findings.title: Profile Photos grid links to /feed#<postId>, but the feed only renders the newest 20 posts — every older photo click dead-ends at the top of the feed
findings.expected: Clicking a photo on someone's profile lands on that photo's post.
findings.actual: page.tsx:293: `href={`/feed#${ph.postId}`}`. The anchor target is `<article id={post.id}>` (post-card.tsx:189), which only exists if the post is in the feed's FIRST page — `const PAGE_SIZE = 20` (feed/actions.ts:762) with cursor-based load-more. The Photos grid pulls from up to 60 of the author's posts across their whole history (page.tsx:151-156, orderBy createdAt desc, take 60), so for any but a very recent post the fragment matches nothing and the browser sits at the top of /feed with no explanation. There is no /post/[id] permalink route and no hash-driven loading in the feed page (grep confirms).
findings.evidence: The only `/feed#` usage in src is this line; feed/page.tsx contains no hash/scrollIntoView/getElementById handling.
findings.fixDirection: Either give posts a real permalink route ( /feed/post/[id] or a modal route) and link the grid there, or make the feed page read location.hash on mount and load pages until the target id is present before scrolling (bounded, e.g. 5 pages, with a fallback message). The former is the durable fix and also serves notifications/deep links.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: seed an author with 25+ posts, open their profile Photos tab, click the oldest photo, assert the viewport ends scrolled to that post (expect.poll on the article's boundingBox), not at the feed top.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: open any member profile whose photo-bearing post is older than the 20 newest feed posts, click it, observe the dead-end.

findings.title: Profile client fetch/submit paths have no rejection handling: a transient failure leaves permanent skeletons, a stuck 'Loading...' button, a stuck photoBusy flag, or a silent no-op
findings.expected: When the DB or network hiccups mid-request the member sees something actionable (an error state, a retry), and busy flags reset.
findings.actual: Four sites: (1) ProfileAuthorFeed mount fetch — `loadPosts({ authorId, kind }).then((data) => {...})` with no .catch; a rejection leaves `loading` true forever: the profile's Posts/Letters tab is a skeleton until reload, plus an unhandled promise rejection. (2) handleLoadMore (lines 67-74) — `const data = await loadPosts(...)` with no try/catch; a rejection leaves loadingMore=true, the button permanently disabled at 'Loading...'. (3) SavedPostsFeed mount fetch (saved-posts-feed.tsx:125-129) — same shape as (1). (4) uploadAvatarBlob (letterhead-profile.tsx:348-360) — `setPhotoBusy(true); ... const result = await updateAvatar(fd);` with no try/catch: a thrown action (network, 413) rejects, photoBusy sticks true (remove/change controls disabled), and NO toast appears; the call sites invoke it as `void uploadAvatarBlob(f)`. FlagPersonDialog.handleSubmit (lines 30-38) similarly leaves `submitting` stuck on a rejection.
findings.evidence: Quoted call shapes above; none of the five sites has a catch/finally that resets its busy state or shows a message.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap each in try/catch/finally: finally resets the busy flag; catch sets an inline error state with a retry affordance (feeds) or a toast ('That did not load/save. Check your connection.') for the dialogs/upload. For the mount fetches, an error state component in place of the skeleton.
findings.gateOrTest: Component tests mocking a rejecting action for each site, asserting the busy flag resets and an error affordance renders.
findings.reproPlan: Live with chrome-devtools: block the server-action request (network conditions offline) while opening a profile's Posts tab — skeleton persists indefinitely with a console unhandled-rejection.

findings.title: Undecodable-photo fallback ships the ORIGINAL file (allowed up to 15MB) through a server action capped at ~4.5MB: a large HEIC dies at the platform with no message instead of the friendly 'export as JPG' answer
findings.expected: The crop dialog exists precisely because 'a 6MB phone photo could die on Vercel's ~4.5MB serverless body cap' (letterhead-profile.tsx:363-365). Every upload path should stay under the cap or use presign.
findings.actual: handlePhotoPick allows any image up to 15MB (line 369: `if (f.size > 15 * 1024 * 1024) return toast.error(...)`). When the browser cannot decode the file (HEIC on Chrome/Android — common for iPhone-exported photos), AvatarCropDialog's onDecodeError hands the ORIGINAL File back: letterhead-profile.tsx:1269-1275 `onDecodeError={(f) => { ...; void uploadAvatarBlob(f); }}` — 'Send the original to the server, whose sharp pipeline either handles it or answers with the friendly "export as JPG" message'. But updateAvatar is a plain server action (FormData through the function body), so a HEIC over ~4.5MB is rejected by Vercel with a 413 before the action runs; the friendly message never sends, the action call rejects, and (per the finding above) photoBusy sticks with no toast. MAX_AVATAR_INPUT = 15MB (settings/actions.ts:20) documents an input size the transport can no longer carry.
findings.evidence: Quoted lines; there is no presign path in updateAvatar (it reads `formData.get("file")` directly).
findings.fixDirection: Cap the fallback: in handlePhotoPick or onDecodeError, if the undecodable file exceeds ~4MB, show the 'export as JPG or PNG' guidance client-side instead of attempting the upload (the server's message for HEIC is already known text); or route the fallback through the existing presigned direct-upload path and process server-side from R2. Also align MAX_AVATAR_INPUT with what the transport actually permits for the direct-action path.
findings.gateOrTest: Component test: onDecodeError with a 6MB fake file asserts no server call and a visible message. Manual E2E once: upload a >4.5MB HEIC from Chrome.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test account: craft a 6MB file with a .heic type (or a real iPhone HEIC), pick it as profile photo in Chrome — observe the silent failure and stuck busy state.

findings.title: The deletion-cancelled notification links to /settings, a route that no longer exists — the member who just rescued their account clicks it and lands on a 404
findings.expected: The 'Welcome back. Your account was scheduled for deletion; signing in has cancelled that...' notification links somewhere real (the profile, or /feed).
findings.actual: auth.ts:185-192 creates the notification with `link: "/settings"`. The settings route was deleted when the profile became the edit surface (letterhead-profile.tsx:125-127: 'Nothing sets it now that /settings is gone'; sidebar.tsx:544-545: 'There is no settings page any more'). find over src/app shows no settings directory and next.config.ts has no redirect for it, so the link 404s inside the app. This fires at an emotionally loaded moment (deletion just cancelled) for exactly the member most likely to distrust the product.
findings.evidence: auth.ts quoted; `find src/app -type d -name "settings*"` returns nothing; grep of next.config.ts redirects/rewrites shows only /ingest PostHog rewrites.
findings.fixDirection: Point the link at `/profile/${user.id}?edit=1` (the settings successor) or `/feed`. Sweep for other literal "/settings" links while there (admin analytics presence map also still names it, cosmetic).
findings.gateOrTest: Add a unit check (or extend the lab route-audit) that every `link:` written into Notification rows resolves to a route in the app's route manifest.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: navigate to /settings signed in — observe the 404. (Provoking the notification itself would require a deletion request on a test account; the dead route alone proves the link.)

findings.title: /api/account/export streams the member's entire history unbounded in one JSON response — a prolific member's export can exceed Vercel's ~4.5MB response cap and fail outright
findings.expected: The GDPR export succeeds for every member regardless of volume.
findings.actual: Every query is unbounded: `prisma.post.findMany({ where: { authorId: userId }, ... select: { content: true, images: true, ... } })`, likewise comments, likes, photos, catchupEntries, adminMessages (route.ts:87-135) — no take anywhere — then `JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)` (pretty-printed, roughly +30% bytes) into a single NextResponse. Post.content is capped at 20,000 chars (postSchema), comments at 1,000; a member with a few hundred long posts/letters plus comments crosses 4.5MB, at which point the serverless response is rejected by the platform and the member gets a generic failure — and has burned one of their 3/day export tokens (rateLimit is consumed at route.ts:35 before the work).
findings.evidence: Quoted query shapes; response built at route.ts:164-170 as one `new NextResponse(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2))`. The rate limit consumption ordering is at :35-41.
findings.fixDirection: Bound the memory and body: drop the pretty-print (stringify without indentation), and either stream the JSON, paginate the heavy sections into the same file via chunked reads, or generate the export to R2 (a private object with a short-lived signed URL) and respond with the link — which also removes the response-size ceiling entirely. Consider refunding the rate-limit token on failure.
findings.gateOrTest: Load-shaped test: seed a test user with ~300 max-length posts locally and assert the export route still answers; or a unit assertion that the serialized body stays under a stated budget per N rows.
findings.reproPlan: Code-argument plus arithmetic (225 x 20KB posts ≈ 4.5MB before indentation); a live proof would need seeding large volumes and is not worth the shared-DB risk.

findings.title: parseJsonArray(user.phones) has no element-type guard: one non-string element in the phones column crashes the entire profile page server-side for every viewer
findings.expected: Every JSON-in-string reader tolerates an old/manual row (the houses reader parseHouseYearEntries and links reader parseUserLinks both validate element shape and type).
findings.actual: parseJsonArray (utils.ts:28-36) returns `Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : []` — valid JSON arrays pass through with NO element validation, typed as string[]. page.tsx:182 `const parsedPhones = parseJsonArray(user.phones)` then :219 `value: formatPhoneDisplay(p)` where formatPhoneDisplay does `raw.trim()` (utils.ts:127) — a phones column of e.g. `[9876543210]` (numbers, from a manual fix-up or a future writer regression) throws TypeError during server render, 500ing the profile for everyone who views it, including its owner. Malformed JSON is safe everywhere (try/catch → []); the gap is exclusively element type. No current writer can produce non-strings (both writers JSON.stringify normalized string arrays), so the trigger is a legacy/manual row — but the blast radius when it happens is a whole-page crash.
findings.evidence: Quoted lines; contrast parseUserLinks (social.ts:66-76) which filters on `typeof e.label === "string" && typeof e.url === "string"`.
findings.fixDirection: Either make parseJsonArray filter to strings (`parsed.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === "string")` — check its other call sites, they all treat the result as string[]), or add a dedicated parsePhones that mirrors parseUserLinks' shape-checking.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: parseJsonArray('[123, {"a":1}, "+91"]') must yield only strings; a render test of the profile page with a hostile phones row.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (would require writing a malformed row to the shared database).

findings.title: generateMetadata omits the deletionRequestedAt gate the page body enforces: the tab title can carry the name of an account the page pretends does not exist
findings.expected: The page's own rule: 'notFound() (not a 403) so the page never even hints the account exists' (comment at page.tsx:108-111) — applied consistently to the metadata.
findings.actual: generateMetadata (page.tsx:34-39) checks `if (!user || user.isBlocked) return { title: "Profile" }` but not `deletionRequestedAt`, while the page body 404s on all three (line 112). If Next.js applies the resolved metadata around the not-found boundary, a viewer hitting a grace-window member's URL gets a 404 body with the member's name in the tab title — a hint the page body was explicitly built not to give. Needs one live check of what title the 404 renders with.
findings.evidence: The two conditions quoted; the asymmetry is provable from the file alone.
findings.fixDirection: Add `|| user.deletionRequestedAt` to the generateMetadata guard so both paths return the neutral 'Profile' title.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit-level: a test asserting generateMetadata returns 'Profile' for a row with deletionRequestedAt set.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only IF a deletion-requested account exists (unlikely on prod): open its /profile/<id> and read document.title on the 404. Otherwise code-argument.

findings.title: Deletion-scheduled email renders the purge date in server UTC: members acting between 00:00 and 05:30 IST are told a purge date one calendar day earlier than their own
findings.expected: The purge date in the confirmation email matches the member's calendar (members are IST, UTC+5:30).
findings.actual: settings/actions.ts:315 `const purgeAt = new Date(Date.now() + DELETION_GRACE_DAYS * 86_400_000);` then :344-349 `purgeDate: purgeAt.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" })` — no timeZone option, so on Vercel (UTC) it formats the UTC date. A member confirming at 01:00 IST on 1 Sep produces purgeAt = 30 Oct 19:30 UTC; the email says '30 October' while in the member's timezone the moment is 31 October 01:00 — and the nightly sweep will actually purge at its first run after that instant, in IST terms on the 31st. The audit-log detail at :333 (`purgeAt.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`) has the same UTC framing (acceptable for an admin log, wrong for the member-facing mail).
findings.evidence: Quoted lines; DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 60 (account-purge.ts:26); sweep cutoff `deletionRequestedAt < now - 60d` (retention.ts:117).
findings.fixDirection: Format the member-facing date with `timeZone: "Asia/Kolkata"` in the toLocaleDateString options (the audience is IST by product definition), or phrase the mail as '60 days from now (on or shortly after <date>)' to absorb both the timezone and the sweep-schedule slack.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on the purgeDate formatting with a fixed Date in the 18:30-24:00 UTC band asserting the IST calendar date.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (arithmetic is deterministic).

findings.title: Dark-mode tile keys on the DB while the /dark-mode route keys on the device cookie: on a new device a dark-mode member is told 'Turning it off is one press' and then handed the full entry gauntlet
findings.expected: The theme controls describe the state of THIS device consistently (and per theme.ts:42's comment, 'a forgotten device should eventually drift back to the DB truth on next sign-in').
findings.actual: The profile edit tile reads the DB row: letterhead-profile.tsx:1194 `{draft?.theme === "dark" ? "Dark mode is on" : "Dark mode"}` and :1198 'You made it through the questions. Turning it off is one press.' The route it links to gates on the COOKIE: dark-mode/page.tsx:25 `if ((await getThemeCookie()) === "dark") return <LightsOn />;` else the DarkGauntlet. On a device that has never set the cookie, a DB-dark member renders LIGHT (root layout reads the cookie, layout.tsx:68), the tile says 'Dark mode is on... one press', and the link opens the question gauntlet — three mutually contradictory statements on one screen. Nothing syncs the cookie from User.theme at sign-in (grep for theme in auth.ts: zero hits), so the comment's 'drift back on next sign-in' is unimplemented.
findings.evidence: Quoted lines; setTheme (theme-actions.ts:28-44) is the only cookie writer.
findings.fixDirection: Pick one source for the tile: pass the device truth (cookie) into the draft instead of user.theme, so tile, rendering and route agree; separately (optional) implement the promised sign-in sync by setting the rv-theme cookie from User.theme after authorize succeeds.
findings.gateOrTest: E2E: with User.theme=dark and no rv-theme cookie, load own profile in edit mode — assert the tile does NOT claim dark is on, and /dark-mode shows the state-consistent surface.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test account: complete the gauntlet (sets DB+cookie), then clear only the rv-theme cookie in devtools and reload the profile edit view.

findings.title: No cross-field sanity on the year set: yearLeft < yearJoined, batchYear < yearLeft and similar combinations save silently, printing 'In the valley 2020–2010' and deriving a nonsense batchType
findings.expected: A typo'd pair (left before joined; batch year before leaving year) is caught at save, or at least never rendered as a backwards range or a wrong credential.
findings.actual: updateProfileField's year branch (profile-actions.ts:126-134) validates each year only in isolation (1926..2100), and profileSchema (validators.ts:104-106) likewise has no refine across yearJoined/yearLeft/batchYear. Consequences: rvYearsLabel (page.tsx:50) prints `${yearJoined}–${yearLeft}` = '2020–2010'; batchTypeFromLeaving (utils.ts:250-258) computes `12 - (batchYear - yearLeft)` — batchYear 2015 with yearLeft 2023 yields grade 20 → 'ISC' silently stored; the houses editor collapses to its fallback sentence because `yearLeft - 1 >= yearJoined` fails (house-chain-editor.tsx:121-124), so the member also loses the chain with no hint the years are the reason. Also note the inline editor allows years to 2100 while the (currently caller-less) profileSchema caps at currentYear+1 — a divergence to collapse when touching this.
findings.evidence: Quoted lines; no refine/cross-check exists in either writer.
findings.fixDirection: In updateProfileField's year branch, after computing the new value, read the counterpart(s) (it already fetches batchYear/yearLeft for the batchType derivation) and reject pairs where yearLeft < yearJoined or batchYear < yearLeft with a plain sentence ('The year you left can't be before the year you joined.'). Keep the check symmetrical so fixing either field clears it.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit tests on updateProfileField for the two inverted pairs expecting { error }; a render test that rvYearsLabel never receives an inverted pair.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test account: set yearJoined 2020 then yearLeft 2010 in the inline editor; observe '2020–2010' on the sheet and the houses section replaced by the fill-in prompt.

findings.title: The generated vCard is spec-non-compliant: LF line endings instead of CRLF and unescaped commas/semicolons in FN/ADR/NOTE (gazetteer city labels contain commas), so strict contact apps may import it mangled
findings.expected: 'Save contact' produces a .vcf that iOS/Android contact apps import with fields intact.
findings.actual: page.tsx:270-284 builds the card with `.join("\n")` — RFC 2426/6350 require CRLF line delimiters — and interpolates raw values: `ADR:;;${c};;;;` where c is a UserPlace label like 'London, England, United Kingdom' (commas are multi-value separators inside a vCard component and must be backslash-escaped), and `NOTE:${batchLine(user)}, Rishi Valley community${houseNote}` with unescaped commas/semicolons. Lenient parsers cope; stricter ones split the city into multiple values or mis-parse the note. A member's name containing a comma (rare) would likewise corrupt FN.
findings.evidence: Quoted construction; cityLabels come from `user.places.map((p) => p.label)` (page.tsx:168-170), and UserPlace labels are stored as the disambiguated picker strings (normalize.ts shortPlaceLabel's comment: 'The gazetteer stores labels such as "London, England, United Kingdom"').
findings.fixDirection: Escape per vCard 3.0 (backslash-escape , ; \ and newline in text values), join with \r\n, and consider using the short city (`p.city`) in ADR instead of the long label.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on the vcard string: assert CRLF delimiters and escaped commas for a fixture user with a multi-part city label.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: download a Save-contact card for a member with a comma-bearing city and import into macOS Contacts / an Android device; inspect the address field.

findings.title: Admins get notFound() for blocked members' profiles too, so the profile's own block control is one-way: block someone from their sheet and the page (with the unblock toggle and admin note) becomes unreachable
findings.expected: An admin can still open a blocked member's profile (where AdminProfileTools renders the unblock control and the admin note).
findings.actual: page.tsx:112 `if (!user || user.isBlocked || user.deletionRequestedAt) notFound();` applies to every viewer including admins (isAdmin is computed at line 120, after the gate). adminBlockUser even does `revalidatePath(`/profile/${userId}`)` (admin-actions.ts:40) — the page the admin is standing on 404s on its next render. Unblocking requires knowing to go to /admin/people; the isBlocked/adminNote props passed to AdminProfileTools from this page are dead-true-branches. Not member-facing, but a real workflow dead-end for the one admin (the owner).
findings.evidence: Quoted gate ordering; AdminProfileTools receives isBlocked (page.tsx:344-350) yet can only ever render with isBlocked=false here.
findings.fixDirection: Let admins through: `if (!user || ((user.isBlocked || user.deletionRequestedAt) && session.user.role !== "admin")) notFound();`, ideally with a visible banner ('This account is blocked / scheduled for deletion') so the admin knows what they are looking at.
findings.gateOrTest: E2E as admin: block a seeded member, revisit their profile, assert the sheet renders with the unblock control instead of 404.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only against production; provable live on the demo/seed environment by blocking a seeded member.

findings.title: parseHouseSpans merges same-house entries across an unrecorded gap year, so the profile asserts a span covering a year the member never answered and the editor's grey pill lands out of chronological order
findings.expected: A member with Aravali recorded for 2014 and 2016 but nothing for 2015 shows two one-year Aravali pills with the unanswered year between them; a span label only covers years actually recorded.
findings.actual: parseHouseSpans (house-spans.ts:152-163): after sorting, `if (last && last.house.toLowerCase() === entry.house.toLowerCase() && entry.year >= last.toYear) { last.toYear = entry.year; }` — the condition is always true for any later same-house entry (entries are sorted ascending), so 2014-Aravali and 2016-Aravali collapse into ONE span rendered 'Aravali 2014-17', claiming the unanswered 2015-16 academic year. In the editor this compounds: firstGap finds 2015, but `indexOfYear(spans, 2015)` ('before the first span that starts later', house-chain-editor.tsx:354-357) finds no span starting after 2015 and places the grey 2015-16 pill AFTER the merged span — contradicting the code's own promise that 'clearing a year in the middle of a finished chain has to put the grey pill back where that year belongs'. Reachable in two clicks: chain Aravali/Ganga/Aravali across 2014-16, tap the Ganga pill, toggle Ganga off — the two Aravali pills instantly fuse into a three-year span with the grey pill dangling at the end.
findings.evidence: Quoted collapse condition (`entry.year >= last.toYear` cannot be false post-sort, so only the house-name check gates merging — gap size is never consulted); indexOfYear quoted.
findings.fixDirection: Make the merge require adjacency-or-repeat: `entry.year <= last.toYear + 1` (a repeated year still merges, a gap opens a new span). indexOfYear then places the mid-chain grey pill correctly with no further change.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit tests on parseHouseSpans: [{2014,A},{2016,A}] → two spans; [{2014,A},{2015,A}] → one span 2014-16 label; [{2014,A},{2014,A}] → one.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test account: build the 3-year chain, remove the middle house, screenshot the fused pill and trailing grey pill.

verifiedClean: 6c-authz-on-every-action: every action in settings/actions.ts, profile-actions.ts, theme-actions.ts, onboarding saveOnboardingHouses and the export route re-checks the session first and pins the write to session.user.id; updateProfileField additionally whitelists columns (EDITABLE_FIELDS) and gates teacher-only fields on the ROW's accountType — no IDOR/mass-assignment path found (consistent with the closed security audit)

6c-revalidation: profile writes revalidatePath the profile (and the client adds router.refresh()); theme deliberately revalidates nothing with a sound argument; no stale-cache surface found beyond the client-state nuances already reported

6d-transactions: updateUserPlaces uses one array $transaction (delete+recreate atomic); purgeUserAccount wraps report-clearing + user.delete in one $transaction; no interactive $transaction held across network calls in this territory; no SET/advisory-lock/pgbouncer-hostile feature used

6e-credentialVersion: requestAccountDeletion bumps the epoch (ends all sessions); adminBlockUser bumps on block AND unblock; session callback re-reads the row each request so name/photo/verifyState never go stale; deletion-grace sign-in cancels the request and is awaited before session mint

6h-json-reader-guards: houses (parseHouseYearEntries) and links (parseUserLinks) both validate element shape and type and cap lengths on read; malformed JSON returns [] in every reader including purge collection — the only element-type gap is phones (reported)

6h-writer-caps (M18): both contact writers (updateUserProfile's profileSchema, updateContactMethods' contactMethodsSchema) cap displayEmail/phones(5)/links(10, https-only, label 60, url 300); saveOnboardingHouses caps 60 rows x 60 chars with year bounds; avatar upload caps size, sniffs bytes, and normalizes to 512px WebP

6j-bounded-queries: profile page counts are batched (Promise.all), photos take 60, saved posts take 120, author feed pages at 20 with cursor; no N+1 loops over prisma in these components; export is member-scoped (volume issue reported separately)

6g-avatar-flow-ordering: updateAvatar writes the new URL before best-effort-deleting the old (correct order — a failed delete can never break rendering); removeAvatar nulls before deleting; delImage/keyForUrl refuse foreign URLs and traversal; rapid double-upload race can orphan at most one object (noted, below reporting bar)

double-submit-guards: deletion dialog (deleting flag + disabled + password-length gate), crop dialog (confirming flag, dismissal ignored mid-save), Load more (disabled while loadingMore), export (3/day sliding limit), avatar (uploads 40/h limiter) — all present

export-privacy: the export selects only the member's own comments/likes/posts/photos/messages; no other member's content (e.g. comments on my posts) is included; operational columns (password hash, credentialVersion, adminNote) excluded
admissionNumber-exposure: rendered per the owner's public-but-understated decision, consistently across read-only lockup, editable colophon and export; no gate asymmetry found

coverPhoto-stale-pointer (territory question): User.coverPhoto currently has NO reader and NO writer outside the export dump and lab mocks (settings-form.tsx is deleted), so a cover pointing at a deleted/hidden Photo is unreachable today — vestigial column, not a live bug

house-spans-arithmetic: end-exclusive [yearJoined, yearLeft) convention is consistent across seedHouseYearRows, missingYears, restoreAllYearRows and the editor's career bounds; the legacy inclusive-range leaving-year row is deliberately dropped; academicSpanLabel century wrap ((toYear+1)%100 padded) verified for 1999→'1999-00'

avatar-determinism: species/colour/pose all pure FNV-1a over the id (no Date/random/locale), Hoopoe remap and Roller reservation both enforced in resolveBirdOverride with the pin wrapped against DRAWN_SPECIES_COUNT; photo>override>pin>hash precedence consistent between PerchedBird's chip and BirdAvatar

retention-sweep-idempotency: every step is a hard-cutoff deleteMany, safe under double-fire; a second concurrent purge of the same user fails closed inside purgeUserAccount's catch; per-step try/catch keeps one failing table from stopping the rest
theme-action-validation: setTheme re-validates the enum server-side before DB/cookie writes; cookie parse rejects anything but light/dark
coverageNotes: Read whole: docs/spec/profile.md, settings/actions.ts (WIP state), profile-actions.ts, letterhead-profile.tsx (all 1816 lines), houses-chain.tsx (all 864), house-chain-editor.tsx, contacts-editor.tsx, pen.tsx, saved-posts-feed.tsx, profile-author-feed.tsx, get-in-touch.tsx, avatar-crop-dialog.tsx, theme-actions.ts, profile/[id]/page.tsx, account-purge.ts, retention.ts, export route, sweep route, avatar.ts, theme.ts, mask-email.ts, house-spans.ts, houses.ts, social.ts, normalize.ts, validators.ts (profile/contact schemas), rate-limit.ts (WIP), member-gate.ts, content-view.ts, storage.ts, dark-mode/page.tsx, root layout theme wiring, relevant slices of feed/actions.ts (loadSavedPosts, loadPosts page size), onboarding/actions.ts (houses save), admin-actions.ts, auth.ts (authorize/session callbacks, WIP), schema.prisma (User/AdminThread/AdminMessage/Photo/Group/UserPlace relations), utils.ts (parseJsonArray, batchLine, formatPhoneDisplay, batchTypeFromLeaving). Skimmed only: flag-person-dialog (top half read; reportUser action belongs to the posts territory), admin-profile-tools.tsx (props-level; its actions read in full), bird-avatar.tsx/bird-avatar-v2.tsx (precedence chain and resolveBirdOverride only — the 50 SVG species are visual), stray-hair/admission-stamp/profile-avatar (decorative), avatars.md spec (superseded-by-code notes in profile.md covered the delta). Consciously skipped as other territories: the catchups round page WIP, directory/where.ts, places/users search API routes, feed internals, upload/presign routes, welcome wizard. Not reported after examination: updateUserProfile in settings/actions.ts is caller-less dead code (its divergent caps — admissionNumber max 10000 vs the inline editor's 100000, name max 100 vs 80 — have no live path; flag for the fix session to delete rather than fix); void recordView is un-awaited during RSC render (accepted-lossy telemetry — subsequent awaited queries almost always cover it; after() would make it certain); auth() triggers a fresh User read per call and the profile page calls it ~3x per view (app-wide pattern, flagged for whichever investigator owns auth/scale); updateProfileField's batchType derivation is a read-modify-write without transaction (two concurrent year edits could stale-derive batchType — window is milliseconds and self-heals on next edit, below the reporting bar); ContactsEditor's module-level id counter (`let seq`) differs server/client across warm lambdas but ids never reach the DOM, so no observable hydration defect. The three High findings (contacts stale-closure, email-removal fallback, purge R2 completeness) are the ones I would fix before release.
